synthesis:
Graph-based fraud detection has matured significantly since this synthesis was first written. [[xu2022graph]] established that heterogeneous GNNs on account–merchant bipartite graphs outperform tabular baselines by 12–18 pp AUC-PR, and subsequent work has refined both the architectural choices and the operational constraints. [[zhang2022fraudre]] extends the relational graph approach to e-commerce fraud with a relation-aware aggregation scheme that is robust to label noise from disputed transactions, and [[dou2020enhancing]] introduces camouflage-resistant neighbor aggregation to counteract fraudster evasion strategies.

The tabular baseline literature has also progressed. [[carcillo2018scarff]] demonstrates that streaming retraining of lightweight classifiers substantially closes the gap with static GNN models in high-drift environments, suggesting that the appropriate architectural choice depends strongly on the velocity of concept drift in the target deployment context.

The emerging consensus is that hybrid systems — a fast tabular scorer for real-time decisioning combined with a periodic GNN batch job for account-level risk scoring — outperform either approach in isolation on production metrics. This architecture is now documented in at least two independent industry deployments referenced in the wiki.

fragments.title: Hybrid tabular + GNN systems outperform either architecture alone on production fraud metrics
Streaming retraining of tabular models substantially closes the recall gap with static GNNs in high-drift environments
Camouflage-resistant neighbor aggregation counteracts fraudster evasion of GNN detectors
